daten.abkommen.klausel.zoll.label: Cut tariffs, open market access
daten.abkommen.klausel.zoll.text: Turkish tariffs on the partner's goods are dropped; domestic producers have to face the competition.
daten.abkommen.klausel.zoll.kehrseite: Domestic producers come under price pressure, above all small and mid-sized firms.
daten.abkommen.klausel.transit.label: Transit and corridor rights
daten.abkommen.klausel.transit.text: The partner's rail, roads and pipelines may run through Turkish territory and Turkish ports.
daten.abkommen.klausel.transit.kehrseite: Transit ties up facilities and creates dependence on the neighbour.
daten.abkommen.klausel.meerengen.label: Commitment on the Straits (Montreux)
daten.abkommen.klausel.meerengen.text: Ankara reaffirms that it will govern the Bosporus and the Dardanelles under the Montreux Convention and let no warships of the belligerents through.
daten.abkommen.klausel.meerengen.kehrsei: Limits freedom of action on the Bosporus; one side always feels short-changed.
daten.abkommen.klausel.militaerzugang.te: Instructors, port calls and access to bases for the partner's armed forces.
daten.abkommen.klausel.militaerzugang.ke: Foreign troops and instructors on home soil; third countries react.
daten.abkommen.klausel.ruestung_koop.tex: Joint development and deliveries of Turkish systems such as drones, ships and tanks.
daten.abkommen.klausel.ruestung_koop.keh: Deliveries to parties in a crisis cost reputation and attract rivals.
daten.abkommen.klausel.ruestung_kauf.tex: Türkiye buys aircraft, engines and spare parts; Ankara pays, the partner delivers.
daten.abkommen.klausel.ruestung_kauf.keh: Orders abroad weigh on the balance of payments and on the domestic defence industry.
daten.abkommen.klausel.bauauftraege.text: Turkish construction firms build roads, power plants and housing; the state guarantees and co-finances.
daten.abkommen.klausel.bauauftraege.kehr: Turkish construction firms earn the money; the state shares the risks.
daten.abkommen.klausel.visa.label: Easier visas
daten.abkommen.klausel.visa.text: Short-stay visas and business travel become easier; travellers and traders no longer face long procedures.
daten.abkommen.klausel.visa.kehrseite: More travellers mean more checks and, in border towns, more tension.
daten.abkommen.klausel.grenzoeffnung.tex: The closed border is opened and ambassadors are exchanged; rail links and trade can follow.
daten.abkommen.klausel.grenzoeffnung.keh: Nationalists and Türkiye's closest partner, Baku, see betrayal; the border provinces of Kars, Iğdır and Ardahan bear the burden.
daten.abkommen.klausel.vermittlung_zusag: Türkiye offers itself as mediator: Istanbul as the venue, Erdoğan's line to both sides as the tool.
Whoever mediates is judged by both sides on the outcome.
daten.abkommen.klausel.gas_kauf.label: Long-term gas purchase contract
daten.abkommen.klausel.gas_kauf.text: Ankara commits to taking natural gas over several years at an agreed price.
daten.abkommen.klausel.gas_kauf.kehrseit: Ties to one supplier; whoever buys his gas never negotiates quite freely, and third parties threaten sanctions.
daten.abkommen.klausel.investitionen_oef: The partner's investors gain access to industry, infrastructure and ports, with legal protection.
Political influence comes with the capital.
daten.abkommen.klausel.kredit_hilfe.text: Ankara gives the partner loans, reconstruction aid and grants.
daten.abkommen.klausel.kredit_hilfe.kehr: Loans to weaker partners rarely come back, and voters ask why the money doesn't stay at home.
daten.abkommen.klausel.reform_zusage.lab: Reform pledge: judiciary and rule of law
daten.abkommen.klausel.reform_zusage.tex: Ankara pledges to make the judiciary more independent and to comply with rulings; Brussels reviews every year.
daten.abkommen.klausel.reform_zusage.keh: A promise Ankara would have to keep at home; whoever breaks it loses credibility.
daten.abkommen.klausel.reform_zusage.pfl: Judicial reform at level 55 or higher.
daten.abkommen.klausel.sanktionen_umgehu: Turkish firms stop routing goods to Russia through detours; banks check more strictly.
Trade with Russia and exporters' side earnings shrink.
Türkiye secures its borders and takes back irregular migrants.
Those taken back stay in the country for now; pressure on the border provinces grows.
Border protection at level 60 or higher.
daten.abkommen.klausel.s400.label: Deactivate or store the S-400
daten.abkommen.klausel.s400.text: The Russian air defence system is no longer operated: the precondition for ending US sanctions and the way back to the F-35.
daten.abkommen.klausel.s400.kehrseite: Moscow loses a major customer, and at home it is seen as kowtowing to Washington.
daten.abkommen.klausel.zahlungsweg.label: Payment channel via Turkish banks
daten.abkommen.klausel.zahlungsweg.text: Turkish banks process payments that fail elsewhere because of sanctions.
daten.abkommen.klausel.zahlungsweg.kehrs: Secondary sanctions: whoever circumvents Western sanctions becomes a target.
daten.abkommen.klausel.ende_sperre.label: Lift the trade and port embargo
daten.abkommen.klausel.ende_sperre.text: The embargo on trade and shipping ends; airspace remains a separate issue.
daten.abkommen.klausel.ende_sperre.kehrs: For many voters, a break with the stance on Gaza.
daten.abkommen.klausel.v_casus.label: Let the 1995 war threat rest
daten.abkommen.klausel.v_casus.text: The 1995 parliamentary resolution treating an extension of Greek territorial waters to twelve nautical miles as a cause for war is no longer reaffirmed.
daten.abkommen.klausel.v_casus.kehrseite: One less lever in the Aegean; nationalists call it a sell-out.
No exploratory drilling in disputed waters
Drillships stay out of waters in which the partner claims rights.
Gas fields in the Mediterranean stay untapped as long as the boundaries are unresolved.
No expansion of gas production beyond level 55.
daten.abkommen.klausel.hafen_oeffnung.la: Open ports and airports to Cypriot ships and aircraft
daten.abkommen.klausel.hafen_oeffnung.te: Turkish ports and airports are open to ships and aircraft of the Republic of Cyprus, as the Ankara Protocol to the customs union requires.
daten.abkommen.klausel.hafen_oeffnung.ke: Nationalists see it as recognising Cyprus with nothing in return.
daten.abkommen.klausel.wasser.label: Commit to water volumes from the Euphrates and Tigris
daten.abkommen.klausel.wasser.text: The dams in the southeast reliably release water southwards, even when it is scarce.
daten.abkommen.klausel.wasser.kehrseite: Every cubic metre sent downstream is missing in the southeast, especially in drought years.
daten.abkommen.klausel.energie_lieferung: Supply electricity and gas to the neighbour
Lines and grids are connected; Türkiye supplies electricity and gas.
Whatever the neighbour gets is missing at home in an emergency.
daten.abkommen.klausel.beistand.label: Mutual defence obligation
daten.abkommen.klausel.beistand.text: An attack on one partner counts as an attack on all; Ankara commits to helping if it comes to that.
daten.abkommen.klausel.beistand.kehrseit: Mutual defence means troops when it counts. A treaty you can only break once.
daten.abkommen.klausel.seesicherheit.lab: Mine clearance and maritime security in the Black Sea
daten.abkommen.klausel.seesicherheit.tex: Joint forces clear mines and secure shipping lanes in the Black Sea.
daten.abkommen.klausel.seesicherheit.keh: Turkish ships in a crisis zone: a single incident is enough for a crisis with Moscow.
daten.abkommen.klausel.bohrung.label: Turkish exploration and production
daten.abkommen.klausel.bohrung.text: Turkish firms explore for and produce oil and gas on the partner's territory.
daten.abkommen.klausel.bohrung.kehrseite: Disputes with Egypt and Greece over maritime boundaries and sovereign rights.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_zoll.label: Market access for Turkish goods
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_zoll.text: Turkish producers may supply on equal terms; trade barriers fall.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_zoll.kehrseite: A cost for the partner: its producers lose out.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_zollunion.label: Modernise the customs union
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_zollunion.text: The 1995 customs union is extended to services, agriculture and public procurement.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_zollunion.kehrs: Greece and Cyprus have blocked it for years; every move there costs the others something.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_visa.label: Visa-free travel for Turkish citizens
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_visa.text: Short stays in the Schengen area without a visa: the core of what many Turks expect from Europe.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_visa.kehrseite: Brussels demands concessions in return that hurt at home.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_ruestung.label: Access to defence technology
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_ruestung.text: Fighter jets, engines and spare parts: the partner releases what is blocked today.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_ruestung.kehrse: Dependence on the supplier: whoever delivers can also block again.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_sanktion.label: Lift sanctions
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_sanktion.text: The sanctions on Türkiye's defence procurement agency and its supply chains are lifted.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_sanktion.kehrse: In return, the partner demands that Ankara take sides.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_preis.label: Gas price discount
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_preis.text: The supplier lowers the price; for Türkiye a lever against high energy prices.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_preis.kehrseite: A discount gets demanded back next time.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_aufschub.label: Payment deferral for gas bills
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_aufschub.text: Gas bills are deferred; the budget gets breathing room.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_aufschub.kehrse: Deferred money is not saved money; the debt grows quietly.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_swap.label: Loan or currency swap
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_swap.text: The partner provides foreign currency or a swap; the central bank's reserves rise.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_swap.kehrseite: Lenders set conditions; the money is never free.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_pkk.label: Action against the PKK and its offshoots
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_pkk.text: The partner acts against armed groups on its territory and coordinates cross-border operations.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_pkk.kehrseite: A promise that only counts if it is kept; otherwise Türkiye carries the load alone again.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_rueckkehr.label: Accept the return of refugees
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_rueckkehr.text: The partner takes back refugees who want to return voluntarily; Türkiye accompanies the return.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_rueckkehr.kehrs: Return without reconstruction remains just words; without security, few go back.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_stuetzpunkt.tex: Turkish armed forces gain access to ports, airfields and training grounds.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_stuetzpunkt.keh: A base abroad costs money and makes you a target.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_pipeline.label: Use the oil and gas pipeline
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_pipeline.text: The pipeline to the Turkish port is run reliably; Ceyhan remains the export point.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_pipeline.kehrse: A Baghdad dispute over oil revenues quickly becomes a Turkish problem.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_transit.label: Transit for Turkish goods and pipelines
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_transit.text: Turkish goods, pipelines and railways may cross the neighbour's territory.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_transit.kehrsei: Whoever must deliver through foreign land is dependent.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_hafen.label: Port and site rights
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_hafen.text: Turkish operators receive concessions for ports and logistics hubs.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_hafen.kehrseite: Concessions abroad depend on the whims of the government there.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_werk.label: A factory in Türkiye
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_werk.text: A manufacturer builds a plant in Türkiye: jobs and technology instead of imports.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_werk.kehrseite: A plant comes with conditions and suppliers that are not Turkish.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_1915.label: Drop the 1915 recognition campaign
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_1915.text: The partner ends its campaign to have the events of 1915 internationally recognised as genocide.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_1915.kehrseite: A demand that strikes the partner at the core of its memory.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_inseln.label: Demilitarisation of the islands
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_inseln.text: The Aegean islands with demilitarised status are not armed, as the treaties of Lausanne and Paris provide.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_inseln.kehrseit: A red line for Athens: it sees arming the islands as its right to self-defence.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_seegrenze.label: Settlement on maritime boundaries and the continental shelf
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_seegrenze.text: Maritime boundaries, the continental shelf and gas fields are negotiated, not declared unilaterally.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_seegrenze.kehrs: Every compromise at sea looks like giving in at home.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_trnc.label: Equal status for Northern Cyprus
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_trnc.text: The Republic of Cyprus recognises the equality of the two communities; Ankara's goal is a two-state solution.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_trnc.kehrseite: A red line for the Republic of Cyprus; it declares any recognition of Northern Cyprus a violation of UN resolutions.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_direkthandel.te: Goods and travellers from the north of the island may enter the EU without detours.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_direkthandel.ke: Nicosia sees any direct trade as upgrading the division.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_libyen.label: A common line on Libya
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_libyen.text: Coordination instead of proxy rivalry: both sides talk to the same partners in Libya.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_libyen.kehrseit: Whoever coordinates must give up their own advantage in the country.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_getreide.label: Grain and trade corridor
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_getreide.text: Grain and fertiliser move through the Black Sea; ports and insurers are working again.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_getreide.kehrse: A corridor holds only as long as both sides keep still.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_luftraum.label: Open overflight and airspace
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_luftraum.text: Flights may again cross the partner's territory; airlines and cargo benefit.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_luftraum.kehrse: A concession on airspace is read at home as weakness.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_investition_zus: The partner's sovereign wealth funds and banks invest money in Türkiye.
Money from abroad comes with conditions; whoever pays wants a say.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_akkuyu.label: Akkuyu: units 2 to 4, fuel and payment channel
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_akkuyu.text: After unit 1, the issue is the remaining units: the payment channel is secured, fuel for years ahead, and Moscow wants the option on a second plant.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_akkuyu.kehrseit: A power plant in Russian hands: whoever supplies the fuel has the last word.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_handelsziel.tex: Trade grows towards a shared target, plus joint defence production.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_handelsziel.keh: Trade targets are mere wishes as long as tariffs don't fall.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_defizit.label: Balancing the trade deficit
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_defizit.text: Part of the imports is offset by Turkish deliveries; the deficit shrinks.
daten.abkommen.klausel.w_defizit.kehrsei: In return, the partner demands concessions on investment.
daten.abkommen.mindestens.zoll.text: Without basic trust, nobody opens their market.
daten.abkommen.mindestens.meerengen.text: The partner first needs trust before accepting such a commitment.
daten.abkommen.mindestens.militaerzugang: Military closeness requires solid security cooperation.
Cooperation is still too thin for arms deals.
Without first signs of trust, there is no border opening.
daten.abkommen.mindestens.beistand.text: Only close partners promise mutual defence.
daten.abkommen.ausstrahlung.ruestung_koo: Yerevan views Baku's arms build-up with concern.
Moscow sees drone deliveries to Kyiv as taking sides.
Cairo sees Ankara's role in Libya as a counter-move.
Athens views the Turkish presence in Libya and the maritime boundary memorandum with concern.
Jerusalem sees Turkish defence cooperation with Damascus as a threat.
Tehran is watching the arms alliance in the Gulf.
daten.abkommen.ausstrahlung.gas_kauf_at_: Washington takes a critical view of any gas contract with Moscow.
Brussels wants to dry up Russia's energy revenues.
daten.abkommen.ausstrahlung.grenzoeffnun: Baku demands a peace treaty with Armenia first.
Moscow loses a major customer and sees Türkiye in the Western camp.
daten.abkommen.ausstrahlung.ende_sperre_: Some Arab partners read the opening as a signal to Jerusalem.
daten.abkommen.ausstrahlung.beistand_at_: Tehran reads the pact as an alliance against itself.
daten.abkommen.ausstrahlung.w_seegrenze_: Athens fears a deal made over Greece's head.
daten.abkommen.ausstrahlung.ruestung_koo: Athens views the defence axis between Ankara and Cairo with concern.
daten.abkommen.ausstrahlung.transit_at_K: Moscow sees its transit network being bypassed.
daten.abkommen.profil.USA.hebelText: Washington holds the stronger hand: it supplies the technology Ankara needs.
daten.abkommen.profil.EU.hebelText: Brussels is the largest trading partner, but an alliance of 27: every move needs unanimity.
daten.abkommen.profil.RUS.hebelText: Moscow needs Türkiye as its gateway to the West; Ankara needs Moscow's gas and Akkuyu.
daten.abkommen.profil.GRC.hebelText: As an EU and NATO member, Athens has backing that it uses in its dispute with Ankara.
daten.abkommen.profil.IRN.hebelText: War-torn Iran needs Ankara more urgently than the other way round: market, payment channels and mediation towards a ceasefire.
daten.abkommen.profil.SYR.hebelText: Damascus depends on Ankara: reconstruction, electricity and security hinge on Türkiye.
daten.abkommen.profil.IRQ.hebelText: Baghdad needs water from Türkiye and, since Hormuz was closed, the northern corridor for its oil; Ankara needs calm on the border and the pipeline.
daten.abkommen.profil.AZE.hebelText: Baku and Ankara are closely tied, but Baku has the gas and the corridor to the east.
daten.abkommen.profil.ARM.hebelText: Yerevan wants the border and the railway, but not at the price of its memory; after the 2026 election the government is stable enough to wait.
daten.abkommen.profil.SAU.hebelText: The Gulf states have the money; Ankara needs their deposits and contracts.
daten.abkommen.profil.ISR.hebelText: The embargo has pushed trade down to zero; Syria and the Board of Peace for Gaza still make Ankara important to Jerusalem.
daten.abkommen.profil.CHN.hebelText: China is the bigger market, Türkiye the gateway to the West: a trade between equals with a tilt.
daten.abkommen.profil.UKR.hebelText: Kyiv needs Ankara's Straits and drones, and Türkiye's lead role in the maritime security guarantees.
daten.abkommen.profil.GEO.hebelText: Tbilisi needs Türkiye as a market and gateway to the West.
daten.abkommen.profil.EGY.hebelText: Cairo was long a rival; the Strategic Partnership since February 2026 holds, but Libya and the maritime boundaries weigh on it.
daten.abkommen.profil.LBY.hebelText: Tripoli leans on Ankara: troops, training and contracts prop up the government there.
daten.abkommen.profil.KAZ.hebelText: Astana negotiates without haste: it has several partners and commits fully to none.
daten.abkommen.profil.CYP.hebelText: Nicosia is an EU member and uses that backing: no favours without movement from Türkiye.
daten.abkommen.rot.GRC.w_inseln: Athens declares arming the islands its right to self-defence; it will not discuss their status.
daten.abkommen.rot.ARM.w_1915: Yerevan demands recognition of 1915; giving it up would mean selling its memory.
daten.abkommen.rot.CYP.w_trnc: Nicosia does not recognise Northern Cyprus; in its view any two-state solution violates UN resolutions.
daten.abkommen.texte.USA.w_ruestung.labe: Release F-35s, F110 engines and spare parts
daten.abkommen.texte.USA.w_ruestung.text: Washington releases the blocked technology: F-35 fighter jets (Türkiye wants 40), F110 engines for the KAAN fighter, spare parts for the F-16.
daten.abkommen.texte.USA.w_sanktion.text: The sanctions on Türkiye's defence procurement agency over the purchase of the S-400 are lifted.
daten.abkommen.texte.USA.s400.text: The Russian S-400 air defence system is put into storage or deactivated; the US defence act (NDAA §1245) ties the way back to exactly this condition.
daten.abkommen.texte.USA.gas_kauf.label: Buy American LNG
daten.abkommen.texte.USA.gas_kauf.text: Long-term supply contracts for US LNG: part of the gas no longer comes from Moscow.
daten.abkommen.texte.EU.w_zollunion.text: The 1995 customs union is modernised; Greece and Cyprus have so far blocked it.
daten.abkommen.texte.EU.w_ruestung.label: SAFE participation (European defence programmes)
daten.abkommen.texte.EU.w_ruestung.text: Türkiye may take part in the EU's joint defence programmes.
daten.abkommen.texte.EU.w_visa.text: Visa-free short stays in the Schengen area; Brussels ties this to reforms on the rule of law and anti-terror laws.
daten.abkommen.texte.RUS.gas_kauf.label: Extend the gas contracts
daten.abkommen.texte.RUS.gas_kauf.text: The gas contracts with Russia expire at the end of 2026; at stake are around 22 billion cubic metres a year.
daten.abkommen.texte.RUS.w_akkuyu.text: Akkuyu unit 1 has been starting up since June 2026; units 2 to 4, fuel security and the payment channel require an agreement.
daten.abkommen.texte.RUS.transit.label: Türkiye as a gas hub
daten.abkommen.texte.RUS.transit.text: Russian gas flows on via Turkish territory to southern Europe.
daten.abkommen.texte.GRC.v_casus.text: The 1995 parliamentary resolution (cause for war at twelve miles) is no longer reaffirmed; Athens has named this for years as a condition for talks on maritime boundaries.
daten.abkommen.texte.GRC.w_seegrenze.lab: Negotiate the twelve-mile zone and continental shelf
daten.abkommen.texte.GRC.w_seegrenze.tex: Maritime boundaries and the continental shelf are negotiated, not declared unilaterally; the Great Sea Interconnector cable project depends on it.
daten.abkommen.texte.IRN.gas_kauf.label: Extend the gas contract
daten.abkommen.texte.IRN.gas_kauf.text: The contract for about 9.6 billion cubic metres a year expired at the end of July 2026; former BOTAŞ managers consider an automatic five-year extension possible.
daten.abkommen.texte.IRN.w_pkk.label: Action against PJAK
daten.abkommen.texte.IRN.w_pkk.text: Tehran acts against the Kurdish group PJAK on the border.
daten.abkommen.texte.IRN.vermittlung_zus: Ankara mediates on a ceasefire and on issues such as the Strait of Hormuz.
daten.abkommen.texte.SYR.ruestung_koop.t: Turkish instructors and systems for the Syrian armed forces.
daten.abkommen.texte.SYR.energie_lieferu: Electricity and gas via the Kilis–Aleppo line
The Kilis–Aleppo pipeline and power grids are expanded; reconstruction needs both.
daten.abkommen.texte.SYR.w_pkk.label: Keep the SDF integrated
daten.abkommen.texte.SYR.w_pkk.text: The Kurdish-led SDF have been integrated into the Syrian armed forces since August 2026; Ankara wants no independent force to return to the border.
daten.abkommen.texte.SYR.w_stuetzpunkt.t: Turkish bases in northern Syria remain; Damascus has to agree.
daten.abkommen.texte.IRQ.w_pipeline.text: The twelve-month protocol of 27 July 2026 is extended; around 250,000 barrels a day flow today, the goal is a long-term agreement on considerably more.
daten.abkommen.texte.IRQ.transit.label: Development Road
daten.abkommen.texte.IRQ.transit.text: The planned Development Road from Basra to the Turkish border links the Gulf and Europe.
daten.abkommen.texte.IRQ.wasser.text: Baghdad demands fixed outflow volumes from the Turkish dams; so far there are projects without any committed water volume.
daten.abkommen.texte.IRQ.w_pkk.text: Baghdad coordinates action against the PKK on Iraqi territory instead of tolerating military operations.
daten.abkommen.texte.AZE.gas_kauf.text: Gas via the TANAP and TAP pipelines; the 2025 Iğdır–Nakhchivan pipeline is the start.
daten.abkommen.texte.AZE.w_transit.label: Nakhchivan railway and pipeline
daten.abkommen.texte.AZE.w_transit.text: The Kars–Nakhchivan railway and the link via TRIPP connect Türkiye with Baku.
daten.abkommen.texte.ARM.grenzoeffnung.t: Opening the border to third-country nationals and diplomats has been agreed but not implemented; direct flights have existed since 2026.
daten.abkommen.texte.ARM.transit.label: Gyumri–Kars railway
daten.abkommen.texte.ARM.transit.text: The railway between Gyumri and Kars links the two countries.
daten.abkommen.texte.ARM.w_transit.label: Transit via the Zangezur corridor (TRIPP)
daten.abkommen.texte.ARM.w_transit.text: The link to Nakhchivan and Baku runs through Armenian territory; transit in exchange for opening the border is the core of a settlement.
daten.abkommen.texte.SAU.beistand.label: Mecca mutual defence pact
daten.abkommen.texte.SAU.beistand.text: On 7 August 2026, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Türkiye signed a mutual defence pact with a collective defence clause; it is already in force and binds Ankara to help if it comes to that.
daten.abkommen.texte.SAU.ruestung_koop.t: The KAAN fighter jet is in final negotiations; air defence comes on top.
daten.abkommen.texte.ISR.ende_sperre.tex: The trade, port and airspace embargo has applied since 2 May 2024 and was tightened in February 2026 with a certificate stop; Azerbaijani oil keeps flowing via Ceyhan as a grey zone. Ending the embargo is the price for everything else.
daten.abkommen.texte.ISR.vermittlung_zus: Türkiye on the Board of Peace for Gaza
Türkiye is a member of the Board of Peace for Gaza; Jerusalem wants it to keep a low profile there.
daten.abkommen.texte.CHN.w_defizit.label: Balance the trade deficit
daten.abkommen.texte.CHN.w_defizit.text: The trade deficit was around 46.3 billion US dollars in 2025; Ankara demands a balance through tariffs, quotas and investment.
daten.abkommen.texte.CHN.w_werk.label: Plant in Türkiye (BYD)
daten.abkommen.texte.CHN.w_werk.text: A BYD plant in Türkiye was cancelled; Ankara wants a new commitment.
daten.abkommen.texte.CHN.w_swap.label: RMB clearing and swap
daten.abkommen.texte.CHN.w_swap.text: Renminbi settlement has existed since November 2025; a larger swap would support the reserves.
daten.abkommen.texte.CHN.transit.label: Middle Corridor
daten.abkommen.texte.CHN.transit.text: Rail and ports as a land bridge between China and Europe, bypassing Russia.
daten.abkommen.texte.UKR.seesicherheit.l: Mine clearance in the Black Sea (Maritime Component Command)
daten.abkommen.texte.UKR.seesicherheit.t: A joint maritime command was set up in April 2026; mine clearance is its first mission.
daten.abkommen.texte.UKR.vermittlung_zus: Ankara hosts talks and prisoner exchanges in Istanbul.
daten.abkommen.texte.GEO.transit.label: Baku–Tbilisi–Kars railway (BTK)
daten.abkommen.texte.GEO.transit.text: The railway has been running at full capacity since 2 June 2026; expansion continues.
daten.abkommen.texte.GEO.w_hafen.label: Anaklia port
daten.abkommen.texte.GEO.w_hafen.text: Turkish operators want to co-operate the deep-sea port of Anaklia on the Black Sea.
daten.abkommen.texte.EGY.w_handelsziel.t: The Strategic Partnership of February 2026 aims to raise trade from 8 to 15 billion US dollars, plus joint defence production.
daten.abkommen.texte.LBY.w_seegrenze.tex: The 2019 agreement on maritime boundaries in the eastern Mediterranean is reaffirmed; Greece, Egypt and Cyprus reject it.
daten.abkommen.texte.KAZ.transit.label: Middle Corridor across the Caspian Sea
daten.abkommen.texte.KAZ.transit.text: Rail, ports and ships on the Trans-Caspian route, bypassing Russia.
daten.abkommen.texte.CYP.verzicht_bohrun: No drilling in the Cypriot economic zone
Drillships stay out of the area that Cyprus claims as its exclusive economic zone.
